docs.title: Arrival Ritual SOP — The First Ninety Seconds

blocks.text: Arrival Ritual SOP — The First Ninety Seconds

A guest decides how they feel about Solana Cove within ninety seconds of stepping out of their car. This SOP defines exactly what happens in that window. It applies to every arrival, every shift, no exceptions. Memorize it; do not read it off a card in front of a guest.
The arrival ritual is the single most-rated touchpoint in our guest surveys. A flawless arrival recovers a mediocre stay; a clumsy one undermines a perfect one.

items: Doorman greets within 10 seconds of the vehicle stopping. Open the guest's door first, never the driver's.
Use the guest's name if you have the arrivals sheet — returning guests should hear their name before they say it.
Offer a cold eucalyptus towel and a glass of hibiscus iced tea while luggage is tagged.
Escort, do not point. Walk the guest to the lobby; never gesture them toward a desk.
Pre-keyed villa: VIPs and returning guests skip the desk entirely and are walked straight to the room.

blocks.text: Tired red-eye arrivals want speed and quiet. Anniversary couples want warmth and a little ceremony. Families want the kids acknowledged by name. Match your energy to theirs — the ritual is a frame, not a script.

items: Never say 'No problem' — say 'My pleasure' or 'Of course'.
Never say 'You'll have to' — say 'The best way is' or 'May I'.
If you don't know, say 'Let me find out for you right now,' then actually do it.
Print the day's arrivals sheet with VIP and returning-guest flags
Confirm welcome amenities are staged for all flagged rooms
Stock the eucalyptus towel chiller and the iced-tea station
Verify all pre-keyed villas have working keys before the guest lands
Brief the doorman on the three highest-priority arrivals by name

blocks.text: We are not checking people in. We are welcoming them home for a week. — Marcus

The night audit closes the financial day, rolls the business date, and prepares the property for the morning team. This runbook is the authoritative order of operations. Run it the same way every night so that when something is wrong, you know exactly where it broke.
Warning: never roll the business date until every restaurant and spa POS terminal has been closed and posted. A premature roll strands charges in the wrong day and creates hours of reconciliation.

items: Confirm all outlets (restaurant, beach bar, spa, in-villa dining) have batched and closed their POS.
Post room and tax charges; verify no rooms show a zero rate without an authorized comp code.
Settle and reconcile the day's credit-card batch against the PMS folio total.
Resolve any guest-disputed charges flagged during the day; leave a note, never a guess.
Back up the PMS before rolling. No exceptions.
Run the no-show report; charge or release per the reservation's policy.
Roll the business date.
Generate the manager's flash report and the morning arrivals/departures sheets.

blocks.text: Between 01:00 and 06:00 the property belongs to the night team. Keep the lobby music low, the porte-cochère lit, and at least two pre-keyed villas ready for unannounced late arrivals. A guest who lands at 3am and finds a warm room is a guest for life.

items: Medical or safety: call emergency services first, then the Director of Front Office.
Maintenance flood/power: maintenance-hotline channel, then Owen directly.
Security or intoxicated-guest incident: log it in detail, photos if safe, MOD on duty.
PMS backup confirmed before roll
Credit-card batch reconciled to the cent
Morning reports printed and left at the desk
Lobby reset and quiet-hours lighting set

blocks.text: Our signature beach gala seats up to 200 covers on the south lawn with the ceremony at the waterline. This playbook is the end-to-end operational spine for every wedding from the planning call to the last shuttle. It assumes a standard Saturday gala; deviations get documented in the event's own brief.

items: T-30 days: final headcount, dietary matrix, floor plan, and rain-call decision tree locked.
T-7 days: BEO distributed to all departments; tasting and walkthrough complete.
T-2 days: tent, dance floor, and generator staged; lighting focus at dusk.
T-1 day: full setup, table top, and a dry-run timeline read with the couple's planner.

blocks.text: The rain call is made by 10:00 the morning of, jointly by the captain, the planner, and the MOD. Once called, it is final. Indecision after 10:00 is what loses weddings, not weather.

items: Captain (Nadia): owns the timeline and is the single point of contact for the planner.
Kitchen lead: plated-vs-stations call, allergy trays flagged with colored picks.
Bar lead (Tomas): sunset pour timing, signature cocktail count, last call coordination.
Front office: guest-room blocks, late checkouts for the wedding party, shuttle manifest.

blocks.text: Our entire timeline bends around golden hour. First dances and toasts are scheduled so the couple is on the floor as the sun hits the water. Confirm the day's exact sunset time during the T-7 brief and build backward from it.

items: Couple's gifts, cake top, and personal décor boxed and labeled for the suite
Rental count reconciled against the delivery manifest before vendor pickup
Lawn irrigation reset and sand-rake the ceremony site by 02:00
Lost-and-found swept and logged; AV and generator powered down
Post-event debrief scheduled within 72 hours while details are fresh

blocks.text: Two hundred people should feel like the only ones on the coast. That's the whole job. — Nadia

This is the live summer menu for the main restaurant, rolled out at the close of the menu refresh project. Everything here is built around what the headland and the morning boat actually deliver. Specials change daily; this is the backbone.

items: Chilled heirloom tomato & stone-fruit gazpacho, basil oil, toasted almond
Crudo of day-boat hamachi, finger lime, fermented chili, headland sea fennel
Grilled octopus, smoked paprika, white bean purée, preserved lemon
Burrata, charred apricot, wild oregano, sourdough cracker
Whole grilled branzino, salsa verde, charred lemon (deboned tableside)
Saffron risotto, summer squash, headland herbs, aged pecorino
Slow-roasted lamb shoulder, smoked eggplant, pomegranate, mint
Charcoal half-chicken, garlic confit, blistered shishito, jus

blocks.text: Allergen tip: the gazpacho garnish and the burrata cracker both contain tree nuts. Always confirm before plating for a flagged table — the allergy matrix lives behind the pass.

Tomas built the by-the-glass pairings to lean coastal and bright. The branzino wants the Assyrtiko; the lamb wants the Bandol rosé, not a heavy red, in this heat. If a guest insists on a big red with fish, pour it with a smile — our job is their pleasure, not our purity.

items: Fish is day-boat or it is not on the menu. No frozen substitutions, ever.
Produce comes from within 90 minutes of the property whenever the season allows.
Headland foraging is done at dawn by the chef team only — never by guests, for safety and conservation.

blocks.text: 86 list and daily specials are posted in the food-and-beverage channel by 15:00 each day. Read it before every service.

The cellar is the most valuable single room on the property. This guide covers how we store it, pour it, and talk about it. Whether you're a server running a glass or a captain at a gala, the standards here don't change.

items: Cellar holds at 13°C, 70% humidity. Log the readings twice daily; flag any drift over 2°C to the bar manager.
Bottles rest on their sides; standing storage is for service-day only.
Sunlight and vibration are the enemies. The cellar door stays closed and the back stair stays clear.
Present the bottle label-out to the host before opening. State producer, region, vintage.
Pour a taste for the host, wait for approval, then serve ladies first, host last.
White and rosé serve at 10–12°C, reds at 16–18°C — never room temperature on the coast.
Decant reds over ten years old or any young, tight red the guest plans to drink now.

blocks.text: If a guest sends a bottle back, never argue. Replace it, taste the returned bottle yourself to learn, and log genuine corked/faulted bottles for the supplier credit.

Our highest-margin, highest-emotion service window is the sunset pour at the beach bar. Pre-chill the rosé and the Assyrtiko, pre-batch the signature mezcal cocktail, and have the by-the-glass reds open and breathing by 17:00. A guest watching the sun hit the water should never wait for a pour.
Sell the place, not the points. 'This grows on a cliff over the same ocean you're looking at' beats any tasting note.

items: Twice-daily cellar temp and humidity logged
By-the-glass reds opened and noted at start of service
Sunset rosé and Assyrtiko chilled by 16:30
Faulted bottles logged for supplier credit weekly

blocks.text: Twelve years on property taught me one thing: a guest can't always say what makes a room feel right, but they always feel it when it's wrong. This is how we turn a villa so it feels right every single time. New attendants train against this document.

items: Strip and air the room; open the doors to the ocean while you work.
Bathroom first — it's the room guests scrutinize most. Polish glass and chrome to no streaks.
Make the bed with the triple-sheet method; hospital corners, crisp, no wrinkles.
Dust top-down, vacuum last, working backward toward the door.
Final pass at the threshold: stand where the guest will stand and look. Fix what your eye catches.

blocks.text: The threshold look is non-negotiable. Most misses — a crooked lamp shade, a smudge on the mirror, a cushion out of line — are invisible up close and obvious from the door.

items: Beds turned to a 45° fold, slippers placed bedside, blackout curtains drawn.
Lights to evening setting; bedside lamp on, overheads off.
Water carafe refreshed, glasses replaced, amenity (seasonal) on the pillow.
Bathroom reset, fresh towels, mat squared, a single tealight by the tub.

blocks.text: We are a reef-safe, low-waste house. Refill stations replace mini bottles, turndown sweets are unwrapped or compostable-wrapped, and linens are changed on request or every third day, not daily, unless the guest asks. Place the linen card so guests know they're choosing, not being skipped.

Returning guests get their preferences pre-set: pillow type, room temperature, and morning amenity all pulled from the guest profile. If you turn a flagged room and the profile is blank, tell your lead — a missing preference is a missed chance to delight.

items: Threshold look completed on every departure turn
Refill stations topped; no single-use plastics staged
Linen-choice card placed face-up
VIP preferences confirmed against profile before turndown

blocks.text: Salt air corrodes everything it touches, slowly and then suddenly. Preventive maintenance is how we keep the ocean from winning. This runbook lists the recurring sweeps that keep the property running and the guest from ever noticing what we do.
Reactive maintenance on the coast costs roughly four times what prevention does. Every skipped PM sweep is a future emergency with a guest standing next to it.

items: Rinse and inspect all exterior hardware, hinges, and railings for corrosion bloom.
Pool plant chemistry and filter backwash; log every reading.
HVAC condensate lines and coil inspection — salt scale clogs them fast.
Test GFCI outlets in all wet areas and villa hot tubs.
Anode and water-heater inspection across all villas.
Solar array panel clean and inverter output log against expected curve.
Generator load-test under real load, not idle.
Roof and gutter check ahead of any forecast weather.

blocks.text: Hot tubs are our highest guest-safety and highest-complaint risk in one fixture. Chemistry is checked daily, drained and sanitized on the schedule, and any tub out of range is closed with a discreet card and a work order — never left in service 'just until checkout'.

items: Guest-facing in an occupied room: respond within 30 minutes, no exceptions.
Safety (electrical, gas, structural): drop everything, route through maintenance-hotline.
Cosmetic / back-of-house: scheduled into the weekly board.
Weekly exterior corrosion sweep logged
Pool and hot-tub chemistry within range and recorded
Solar output reconciled to expected curve
Generator load-tested this month
Open guest-facing work orders cleared before shift handoff

docs.title: Seaside Spa Relaunch — Treatment Menu & SOP

blocks.text: Seaside Spa Relaunch — Treatment Menu & SOP

A great treatment starts the moment a guest exhales. The relaunch is built around that exhale — a hydrotherapy circuit, a signature menu, and a service standard that protects the guest's silence from arrival to afterglow. This is the working draft for the relaunch team.

items: Tidal Restoration (90 min) — seaweed wrap, scalp work, hot-stone spine release.
Headland Botanical Facial (60 min) — foraged herb steam, marine enzyme resurfacing.
Two-Therapist Synchrony Massage (90 min) — our flagship couples treatment.
Sunrise Movement & Breath (45 min) — guided session on the south lawn before the spa opens.
Warm mineral soak to open the body (10 min).
Steam or sauna (10 min) — guest's choice, never both back to back without a cold step.
Cold plunge (1–2 min) — the contrast is the point; coach first-timers gently.
Heated relaxation loungers and herbal tea to close (open-ended).

blocks.text: Contraindications matter. Pregnancy, cardiac conditions, and recent surgery change or cancel the circuit. The intake form is not a formality — read it before you ever touch a guest.

From the relaxation lounge inward, we speak only when spoken to, and we whisper. Phones are checked at the desk. Therapists confirm pressure and temperature with a quiet word, then let the guest disappear. The afterglow is part of the treatment — never rush a guest off the table.

The relaunch introduces multi-day wellness retreats pairing the circuit with chef Laurent's lighter coastal menu and Tomas's no- and low-alcohol pairings. Cross-department coordination lives in the spa-relaunch project; nothing ships to guests until F&B has signed off on the menu side.

items: Therapist certifications current and on file
Intake and contraindication form reviewed before every treatment
Circuit temperatures logged at open and midday
Retreat menu signed off by F&B before publishing

blocks.text: We are refreshing all 18 oceanfront villas — new soft goods, smart climate controls, and rainfall showers — while protecting occupancy. That last clause is the whole challenge. We renovate in phases so we never go dark and never put a guest next to a construction zone.

items: Soft goods: bedding, drapery, upholstery, rugs — full replacement.
Smart climate controls with per-villa scheduling and guest-app integration.
Rainfall showers and refreshed wet areas with reef-safe refill fixtures.
Re-seal and re-coat all salt-exposed exterior hardware while walls are open.
Phase 1 (villas 1–6): low-occupancy midweek blocks, two villas at a time.
Phase 2 (villas 7–12): continues as Phase 1 villas return to inventory.
Phase 3 (villas 13–18): completed ahead of peak wedding season demand.
Buffer week between phases for snags and deep clean before re-letting.

blocks.text: Warning: noisy work stops at 16:00 sharp and never runs on a confirmed wedding day. Sales & Events holds a veto on the day-of-work calendar during wedding season.

items: Front office: pull renovated villas from sellable inventory and re-merchandise on completion.
Housekeeping: deep-clean and re-stage each villa before it returns to inventory.
Sales & Events: protect wedding-block villas from any active phase.

blocks.text: The long-lead items are the smart-control hardware and the imported soft goods. Both are ordered against the phase calendar with a two-week buffer. If a shipment slips, we re-sequence villas rather than push the whole project — never let one late pallet stall the line.

items: Long-lead climate hardware ordered with buffer
Phase 1 villa blocks confirmed with front office
Wedding-day work blackout dates synced with Sales & Events
Deep-clean handoff checklist agreed with housekeeping

blocks.text: Our goal through shoulder season is to lift RevPAR without surrendering margin to the channels. That means defending rate parity, shifting mix toward direct, and making sure our content out-shines every competitor on every screen a guest sees.

items: Rate parity: our rate is never lower on an OTA than on our own site. Disparities get hunted weekly.
Channel mix: grow direct share each month; OTAs fill the gaps, they don't lead the strategy.
Content: hero imagery, accurate amenities, and review responses on every channel — stale content loses to fresh.

blocks.text: Direct is not just cheaper — it's ours. A direct guest's email, preferences, and loyalty live with us, not behind a channel's wall. Every point of direct share compounds.

items: Member-only direct rate, 8% below OTA, gated behind a free sign-up to stay parity-compliant.
Length-of-stay offers that the OTAs price poorly — third night value-add, not discount.
Geo-targeted promotions for our top three feeder cities during their cold weeks.
Spa and dining bundles that raise total spend without touching the room rate.

blocks.text: Every Monday we pull the pickup report, scan parity across Booking.com and Expedia, and re-forecast the next 90 days. Rate changes are deliberate and logged — we never chase a competitor's flash sale into a margin hole.

The cleanest path to real-time parity is the channel manager that ships with the new PMS. Until that migration lands, parity is a manual weekly discipline. Don't wait for the tool to do the work the spreadsheet can do today.

items: Monday pickup + parity scan completed and logged
Direct share tracked against monthly target
Review responses current on all channels
Hero imagery refreshed for shoulder-season campaign

docs.title: Guest Recovery Playbook — Turning a Miss Into a Memory

blocks.text: Things will go wrong. A late villa, a cold plate, a missed wake-up call. What separates a luxury property from a nice one is what happens next. A well-handled recovery produces more loyalty than a flawless stay. This playbook is how we recover.

items: Listen — let the guest finish completely. Do not interrupt to defend.
Empathize — name the feeling: 'I'd be frustrated too. I'm sorry this happened.'
Apologize — sincerely, once, without excuses or blame.
Resolve — fix the actual problem now, then make a goodwill gesture on top.
Notify — log it so the whole team protects the rest of this guest's stay.

blocks.text: Every front-of-house team member is empowered to spend up to a set goodwill amount per incident without a manager's sign-off. Speed of recovery beats size of gesture. Ask Marcus for the current limit if you're unsure.
Match the Gesture to the Miss

items: Minor delay or inconvenience: a sincere apology and a small in-room amenity.
Disrupted meal or experience: comp the item and offer to make it right that day.
Significant stay disruption: manager involvement, partial recovery, and a personal follow-up.
Never over-comp a guest who just wants to be heard — sometimes the apology is the whole fix.

blocks.text: The recovery isn't done when the guest stops being upset. Flag their profile, brief the next shift, and have a manager check in once more before departure. A guest who leaves feeling cared for after a problem tells more friends than one who never had one.
Nobody remembers the room that was always perfect. Everybody remembers the night we fixed it. — Marcus

items: Incident logged with enough detail for the next shift to act on
Profile flagged so the rest of the stay is protected
Manager check-in before the guest departs
Root cause noted so we fix the system, not just the symptom

docs.title: New Hire Onboarding — Front of House

blocks.text: New Hire Onboarding — Front of House

Welcome to Solana Cove. Your first two weeks shape how you'll see this place for years. This guide walks you through them. The goal isn't to memorize everything — it's to know where to look and who to ask, and to understand the standard we hold.

items: Property tour: every guest-facing space, plus the back-of-house routes guests never see
Shadow a full check-in shift and a full check-out shift
Read the Arrival Ritual SOP and watch it run live three times
Meet your buddy and each department lead by name
Complete PMS basics and the guest-profile training

blocks.text: Week Two — Do It With a Net

items: Run check-ins with your buddy standing by
Handle your first guest request end to end
Practice the Guest Recovery LEARN framework in a role-play
Complete the safety and emergency-procedure walkthrough
Sit in on a morning stand-up and a shift handoff

blocks.text: Tip: the fastest way to look like you've worked here for years is to learn guests' names and use them. Ask your buddy how Priya does it — it's the whole job in one habit.

items: Anticipate, don't react. The best service happens before the guest asks.
Own the problem you're handed, even if you didn't cause it.
Never point — escort. Never 'no problem' — 'my pleasure'.
When you don't know, find out fast. 'Let me find out for you right now.'

blocks.text: SOPs and runbooks live in the Front Office space. Daily handoffs and arrivals run in the front-office channel. Anything urgent and property-wide shows up in announcements. When in doubt, ask in your space channel before guessing — nobody here minds a good question.
You're not learning a job. You're joining a standard. — Priya

We sit on a living reef. Quiet luxury and a healthy coastline are not in tension — done right, they're the same thing. This program covers the solar retrofit, zero-waste laundry, reef-safe amenities, and our path to a recognized eco-certification.

items: Energy: solar retrofit covering a growing share of daytime load, tracked against the inverter curve.
Water & laundry: zero-waste laundry, linen-on-request, and greywater-friendly detergents.
Amenities: reef-safe, refillable, no single-use plastics anywhere a guest can see or touch.
Waste: compost back-of-house, eliminate single-use in F&B, divert from landfill by default.

blocks.text: Reef-safe is a hard line, not a preference. Any product containing oxybenzone or octinoxate does not enter this property — not in the spa, not in the villas, not in the gift shop.

items: Refill stations replace mini bottles in every villa; report any that run low before a guest does.
Linen-choice cards placed so guests opt in to changes — most happily skip a day.
Cleaning products are the approved low-impact line only; never substitute off the shelf.

blocks.text: The eco-certification audit measures real data, not intentions. That's why every pillar above has a log. When the auditor asks 'show me,' we open the logbook, not a brochure. Keep your readings current — the certification is earned in the daily records, not the final inspection.

Guests increasingly choose us partly for this. Front office and the spa should be able to speak to it warmly and accurately — never preachy, never greenwashed. If you're not sure a claim is true, don't make it.

items: Solar output logged daily against expected curve
Refill stations stocked across all villas
Approved reef-safe amenity line verified — no banned ingredients
Certification logbook current and audit-ready

blocks.text: We're moving off the legacy PMS to a cloud platform with an integrated POS, channel manager, and guest app. This is the highest-risk operational project on the calendar — it touches every transaction the resort makes. This plan exists so nobody improvises on cutover night.

Warning: a PMS migration done badly can take down check-in, billing, and distribution at once. We move slowly, we test obsessively, and we keep a paper fallback ready until we've slept through a full week on the new system.

items: Discovery & data mapping: every field in the legacy system mapped to the new one.
Parallel run: both systems live, reconciled nightly, until the numbers match for a full week.
Cutover: planned for the lowest-occupancy window, never during wedding season.
Stabilization: vendor on-site or on-call, daily issue triage, until it's boring.
POS: restaurant, beach bar, spa, and in-villa dining all post to the right folio in real time.
Channel manager: real-time rate parity across Booking.com and Expedia — the OTA team's top ask.
Guest app: mobile check-in, key, and requests routed to the right department.

blocks.text: Guest profiles are sacred — preferences, history, and loyalty must arrive intact. We migrate a sample, hand-verify it against the legacy records, and only then run the full set. No profile gets dropped or merged without a human confirming it. A returning guest who has to re-explain their pillow preference is a migration failure.

items: Parallel-run financials reconciled to the cent for seven consecutive days
All POS terminals posting to correct folios in test
Channel manager pushing parity rates without manual touch
Paper fallback procedures printed and staff drilled
Cutover window confirmed clear with Sales & Events

blocks.text: The guest should never know we changed anything except that everything got faster. — Marcus

The summer menu shipped on time and across all three outlets. Now that it's closed out, here's an honest look at what worked, what didn't, and what we carry into the next refresh. Written while it's fresh so the next chef team inherits the lessons, not just the recipes.

items: Day-boat-only sourcing held all season — the branzino became our signature and never went frozen.
Tomas's by-the-glass pairings lifted wine attach rate noticeably without any upsell pressure.
Cross-outlet rollout meant the beach bar and in-villa menus felt like one kitchen, not three.
The allergy matrix behind the pass cut the near-misses we used to have on busy nights.
We under-forecast the octopus and 86'd it twice on peak weekends — bad look at the price point.
The risotto slowed the pass on full covers; à la minute risotto and a 200-cover gala don't mix.
Two foraged ingredients weren't reliably available; we should have had a named substitute from day one.

blocks.text: Lesson that cost us the most: never put a labor-heavy à la minute dish on the menu without a service-volume stress test. The risotto tasted perfect and nearly broke the pass.

items: Build a par-and-forecast model for low-yield proteins like octopus
Pre-name substitutes for every foraged or single-source ingredient
Stress-test any à la minute dish at gala volume before it ships
Keep the allergy matrix; expand it to the beach bar menu

blocks.text: A menu is a promise you make to a full dining room on the worst night, not the best one. — Laurent

This is the master list of vendors cleared to work on property or supply our outlets. 'Approved' means insured, vetted, and aligned with our standards. If a vendor isn't on this list, they don't come through the gate or onto a plate until they're added. No exceptions, especially during wedding season.

items: Day-boat seafood — daily delivery, our hard 'no frozen' partner. Primary for all outlets.
Headland-adjacent produce farm — within 90 minutes, seasonal allocation.
Wine & spirits importers — Tomas's two cellar suppliers, on net terms.
Specialty pastry & bread — daily, pre-dawn delivery for the restaurant.
Tent, dance floor & staging rental — our gala standard, knows the south-lawn site.
Floral & décor — two vetted studios, both insured for on-property installs.
AV & lighting — sunset-window experienced; carries backup generator.
Generator & power — required for every beach gala over a set headcount.
Pool plant chemicals & service — corrosion-coast experienced.
HVAC & refrigeration — emergency call-out within four hours, contracted.
Solar & electrical — the retrofit partner, also on the PM call list.
Reef-safe amenity & cleaning supplier — sustainability-program approved line only.

blocks.text: Warning: every vendor working on property during an event must show current liability insurance to the captain before setup begins. An uninsured vendor on the south lawn is the kind of risk that ends careers, not just events.

New vendors are added only after insurance verification and a department lead's sign-off. Underperforming or lapsed-insurance vendors are pulled immediately and the team is notified in the relevant channel. Keep this list current — it's the difference between a smooth event and a liability.

items: Insurance certificates current for all active vendors
Wedding-season vendors re-confirmed before peak begins
Lapsed or underperforming vendors removed and team notified
Reef-safe supplier verified against the approved amenity line

docs.title: Solana Cove Brand Voice & Guest Communication Guide

blocks.text: Solana Cove Brand Voice & Guest Communication Guide

Where the Pacific meets quiet luxury. That tagline is also our voice. Everything we write to a guest — a confirmation email, a turndown card, a review response, an SMS — should sound like the same calm, warm, confident person. This guide is how we stay that person.

items: Warm, not gushing. We're glad you're here; we don't shout about it.
Confident, not stiff. We know our property cold and we make it look easy.
Specific, not generic. 'Your villa faces the sunset' beats 'enjoy your stay.'
Calm, always. Even in a recovery email, our voice lowers the temperature.

blocks.text: Quiet luxury means we never have to say 'luxury.' If a sentence is bragging, cut it. The experience does the talking; our words just open the door.

items: Use 'my pleasure,' 'of course,' 'we'd love to.' Avoid 'no problem,' 'you'll have to,' 'unfortunately.'
Use the guest's name early and naturally. Avoid 'Dear valued guest.'
Use plain, sensory language. Avoid hotel jargon, ALL CAPS, and exclamation pile-ups.
One exclamation point per message, maximum. Usually zero.
Email: warm and complete; sign with a real person's name, never 'The Team.'
SMS: short, helpful, and signed. Never marketing-blast a guest mid-stay.
Review responses: thank, acknowledge specifically, and never get defensive in public.
In-room cards: handwritten when the moment deserves it — anniversaries, recoveries, returns.

blocks.text: Before: 'Unfortunately your room won't be ready until 3pm.' After: 'Your villa will be ready by three — until then, the beach bar is yours, on us.'
When you're unsure how something should sound, read it aloud. If it sounds like a brochure or a bot, rewrite it until it sounds like Priya welcoming a returning guest by name.

On a beachfront property, the difference between an incident and a catastrophe is preparation and calm. Every team member, regardless of department, is responsible for knowing these procedures. Read this on your first day and review it every quarter.
Warning: in any life-safety situation, call emergency services first. Notifying a manager is the second call, never the first. No one will ever be reprimanded for prioritizing a guest's safety.

items: Activate the nearest alarm and call emergency services.
Evacuate guests toward the assembly point on the south lawn — never back toward the building.
Front office pulls the in-house guest list to account for every room.
Do not re-enter for belongings; do not use elevators.
Call emergency services; send a runner to guide them in from the gate.
Nearest AED locations: lobby, pool plant, and spa reception.
Stay with the guest; assign someone to clear a path and manage onlookers.
Log everything afterward — times, actions, and who was notified.
Beach flags fly daily; red means closed water, and we enforce it kindly but firmly.
Severe-weather and high-surf protocol moves loungers, closes the waterline, and secures the gala tent.
Hot-tub and pool incidents follow the same medical sequence above — chemistry is checked before reopening.

blocks.text: Power loss triggers an automatic generator transfer; if it doesn't, the night manager calls Owen via the maintenance-hotline immediately. For flooding, kill the affected circuit first, then contain — water and electricity together is the one combination we never improvise around.

items: Know your nearest exit and the south-lawn assembly point
Know the three AED locations by heart
Quarterly safety review completed and signed off
Emergency contact tree current at every desk

blocks.text: This archives last year's low-season program: the deep-clean, the preventive-maintenance sweep, and the staffing wind-down. It's closed and filed here so this year's off-season team starts from what we learned, not from scratch.

items: Full property deep-clean, including the back-of-house areas we can't reach mid-season.
Preventive-maintenance sweep across HVAC, pool plant, and all villa hot tubs.
Exterior corrosion treatment on every salt-exposed railing and fixture.
Generator overhaul and a full load-test under real conditions.

blocks.text: We flexed seasonal roles down without losing our core team or our standard. The lesson: communicate the wind-down calendar early and honestly. The staff who felt respected through the slow months came back sharp for peak season; the ones we surprised did not.

Biggest win: doing the noisy, disruptive maintenance in the dark months meant zero guest-facing disruption during peak. Protect this window — don't let an extended booking erode the off-season work calendar.

items: Start long-lead parts ordering two weeks earlier — we lost time waiting on anodes and filters.
Photograph every 'before' so the certification and capital cases are easier to make.
Overlap the deep-clean and PM teams by a day to hand off open items in person.

blocks.text: Status: archived. This year's off-season readiness should fork this document, not start fresh. The runbook works; the improvements above are the only deltas.
The off-season is when we win the high season. — Owen

messages.text: Morning all! Whoever left the bag of pastries in the break room — you are a hero and I love you ☕️🥐
That was Laurent. He over-foraged again and turned it into croissants.
There is no such thing as over-foraging. There is only abundance 🌿
The almond ones are gone already, just so everyone knows
Night shift never gets the almond ones 😤 the eternal injustice
Diego I will hide two in the walk-in for you. Look behind the lemons.
This is why you're my favorite chef 🙏
Can we make pastry Fridays a thing? Asking for the whole spa team (me).
Seconded. Morale and carbs are deeply connected.
I'll allow it. Pastry Fridays officially endorsed by leadership 😄
Best company in the world honestly 🥹
📢 VIP arrival heads-up: the Hartwell party checks in Thursday for the oceanfront villa block. Repeat guests, anniversary stay. Full white-glove treatment.
Mrs. Hartwell is allergic to lilies — no lilies in any arrangement, villa or restaurant. Please flag to all teams.
On it. I remember them — he takes a cortado at 7am sharp, she does decaf oat. Already noted in the profile.
Housekeeping will do the anniversary turndown setup. Rose petals, champagne, no lilies anywhere. Confirmed.
I'll prep a private tasting menu for the anniversary night. Sending options to Marcus by EOD.
Spa here — I'll hold a couples hydrotherapy slot Friday afternoon in case they want it. Just say the word.
Love this. These are exactly the repeat guests our retention numbers live on. Thank you team 👏
Engineering will double-check the villa hot tub and climate controls before arrival. No surprises.
This is the arrival ritual at its best. Proud of this crew. Let's make it unforgettable ✨
Night handoff 📝 Quiet evening. Villa 12 late arrival came in at 1am, all settled. One noise complaint from suite 304 about the wedding afterparty — resolved, moved them to a quieter wing.
Thanks Diego. Did 304 want anything as a recovery gesture?
I comped breakfast and sent a fruit plate. They were happy by the time I left.
Nicely handled. Let's also drop a handwritten note from me. Priya can you set that up?
Already drafting it ✍️ Will have it on their door before checkout.
Heads up — we're at 96% occupancy tonight. Only 3 rooms left and two are oceanfront villas under reno.
Tight. Coordinate with housekeeping on turn times so we don't bottleneck check-in at 3pm.
I'll prep the late-arrival villas tonight so the morning team isn't scrambling.
You're a lifesaver. Also the Hartwell cortado machine — can someone confirm the lobby espresso station is stocked? 7am sharp incoming 😅
I'll check it personally tonight. That cortado will be flawless.
Logging off, see you all on the flip 🌙
Morning team 🧺 Big turn day — 11 checkouts, 14 arrivals, and we need oceanfront villas 3, 5, and 7 deep-cleaned post-reno before 3pm.
On it. I'll put Mariela and the new trainee on the villas, they're the priority. The rest of us take the suites.
Perfect. Reno dust is brutal — make sure they wipe down the new climate control panels gently, no harsh spray.
Noted. Also we're low on the reef-safe amenity sets again. Down to maybe 20 kits.
Ugh, the vendor's behind again. I'll chase them. For now prioritize kits for the villas and VIP rooms.
Will do. Hartwell villa gets the full anniversary turndown right? Petals + champagne, no lilies?
Exactly. And double-check no lily in the standard arrangement — swap for orchids.
Orchids it is 🌸 I'll do that villa myself, want it perfect.
That's why you're the lead. Trainee doing okay on turndowns?
Getting there! Her hospital corners are improving. By end of week she'll be solid.
Love to hear it. Keep me posted on the amenity restock 🙏
Service lineup for tonight 🍽️ 86 the branzino — supplier shorted us. Pushing the line-caught snapper as the special instead, headland herb crust.
Snapper pairs beautifully with the Albariño we just got in. I'll feature it by the glass tonight.
Perfect. Also we have the Hartwell anniversary tasting — 5 courses, no lilies on the plate or table, she's allergic.
I'll handle their table personally. What time seating?
8pm, the corner banquette with the sunset view. Tomas, can you do a pairing flight for them?
Already planning it. Closing with the small-batch mezcal and a dark chocolate course. They'll remember it 🍫
Reservations update — we're fully booked 7-9pm, 84 covers. Beach bar also slammed with the wedding overflow.
Staff up the line then. Nadia can you pull one from banquet to help expo?
Yep, banquet prep is ahead of schedule for tomorrow's gala. I'll send Marco over at 6.
Reminder the new beach bar cocktail menu drops tonight too. The mezcal sunset is going to fly 🌅
Big night. Let's make it clean. Pre-shift at 5, everyone there 🙏
💒 Saturday beach gala — final count is 180 confirmed, ceremony 4pm, reception 6pm on the south lawn. Let's run through readiness.
Banquet's locked. Tables, linens, and the dance floor go down Saturday morning. I need the tide chart confirmed for the ceremony arch placement.
Low tide is 3:40pm Saturday — wait, I'm not in this channel for tide charts but I'll grab it for you 😄 arch will be safe at the 4pm line.
Ha, thanks Owen. Marcus, guest rooms blocked for the wedding party?
All 40 rooms confirmed, welcome bags being prepped by Priya's team. Late checkout granted for the couple's suite.
Menu's finalized — passed canapés, three-course plated, and the late-night taco station the bride wanted. Two vegan, four GF, one shellfish allergy flagged.
Bar's set. Signature cocktail is a hibiscus paloma, plus the champagne tower for the toast. I'll need two extra bartenders for 180.
I'll pull bartenders from the on-call list. Tomas send me names by Thursday.
Rain contingency? Forecast shows a 20% chance Saturday evening.
Tent's on standby, can be up in 90 min. I'll make the call by 2pm Saturday based on radar.
If we tent, I move the taco station under the pergola so it stays dry. Already planned.
This is why we close seven-figure seasons. Incredible work all 🥂 Final walkthrough Friday 3pm, south lawn.
I'll be there. Let's give this couple the wedding of their lives 💍
🔧 Urgent-ish: villa 14 guest reporting the hot tub won't heat. They're checking in at 2pm and specifically booked for it.
On my way. Probably the heater element again, that unit's been temperamental. Give me 30 min to diagnose.
If it's the element we have a spare in the shop. Kenji confirm and I'll pull it.
Confirmed — heater element's fried. Bringing the spare. Should be heated and ready by 1pm, well before the 2pm check-in.
Nice. That's the third element on that unit this season. Flagging it for full replacement in the reno scope.
You two are fast. Front desk owes you a coffee ☕
While you're in villa 14 — guest also mentioned a slow bathroom drain. Can you peek?
Already on it, snaked it. Hair clog, cleared. Drain runs clean now.
Outstanding. Guest will never know there was an issue. That's the standard 👏
Hot tub's heating now, 102°F target. I'll swing back at 1 to confirm temp before I close the ticket.
Great work Kenji. Logging the element pattern — three failures means we replace the whole heater next reno phase. Adding to the budget line.
Ticket can close on my end. Thanks team, crisis averted 🙌
